_comment: Registered regenerable regions for the Kubernetes Go-to-Rust port, plus the origin classification of every first-party crate leaf in the two capabilities the port seam runs between. ADR-637 D2, live via ADR-0704: output in a registered regenerable region is emitted by the registered producer and is NEVER hand-edited; a red result is an engine, rule or policy defect, never repaired by editing emitted Rust. `regions` is EMPTY and stays empty until a PRODUCER exists, which is not the same claim as the engine path being absent: build/port-engine/core/port-engine-kernel IS on the tree (7 tracked files, 924 lines) and registers no producer -- it is a W0 skeleton with no front end, no rule data and no renderer -- while specs/port-rules is genuinely absent and specs/k8s-port/scope.json reports no package enumeration has run. A consumer must be able to tell 'engine present, not yet a producer' from 'engine absent'. The value of this file today is the DENOMINATOR, not the numerator. A boundary partition that classifies leaf by leaf reports the same clean result over an empty region set whether the corpus is genuinely clean or the walk collapsed and saw nothing; enumerating every existing leaf as first-party is what makes that zero honest instead of vacuous. Contract: docs/programs/k8s-port/seam/os-k8s-seam-mapping.md, sections 3.1, 5 and 6.

clauses: ADR-637 D2 — output in a registered regenerable region is generated: emitted by the registered producer, never hand-edited.

ADR-638 D1 — generated Kubernetes Rust output SHALL live under k8s/; os/, cloud/cloud-k8s and the managed-Kubernetes facades consume it only through approved k8s/ports/** seams and MUST NOT become alternate homes for generated upstream code.
ADR-638 D6 — the os/ shared-types direction is deferred to W0-G. This file classifies and predicts placement; it authorizes NO runtime edge and creates no crate.
authority.citation_convention: ADR ids are written as bare text on purpose. docs/decisions/ holds only the live apexes, so any other id written as a path under that directory is a broken link scored against an equality-pinned census; a bare id in a value costs nothing on either census.

regions_state.statement: No regenerable region is registered. Nothing in the repository emits Kubernetes Rust output, so no path is under producer ownership and every byte under k8s/ and os/ is legitimately hand-edited today.
evidence: build/port-engine/core/port-engine-kernel present (7 tracked files) but registers no producer: an ADR-0637 D4 W0 seam skeleton with no source-language front end, no rule data and no renderer, so it emits no output and owns no path.
regions_state.admission_rule: A region may be registered only in the same change as the producer that emits it and the six-axis receipt binding pin, snapshot_digest, engine_digest, rulepack_digest, toolchain_digest and formatter_digest. Registering a path prefix without a producer would forbid hand edits to bytes that nothing can regenerate, which converts a live surface into an unmaintainable one.
regions_state.overlap_rule: Region path prefixes are disjoint. Two regions claiming the same path make the no-hand-edit owner ambiguous, and an ambiguous owner is an unenforced one.

emit_predicate._comment: Section 3.1 of the seam mapping, encoded as data. The upstream package path decides the emit face mechanically; there is no per-package human judgement and therefore nothing for a lane to negotiate. Resolution matches the contract already landed in specs/k8s-port/scope.json: all selectors within a rule match conjunctively, a subject resolves to the matching rule with the highest specificity_rank, and equal highest ranks are an error rather than a tie-break.
emit_predicate.subject: SourceModel package path at the upstream pin recorded in specs/k8s-port/upstream-pin.json
emit_predicate.state_note: Encoded now so parallel units converge on one answer. Nothing evaluates this predicate today; the first evaluator is the producer, which does not exist.

rules.rationale: Vendored and generated upstream inputs are already ruled EXCLUDE by the landed W0-A scope rules. This file does not restate those rules and must not contradict them; the row exists so that resolution is total rather than falling through to the default face.

Upstream itself declares staging/src/k8s.io/* the externally consumable set, published read-only with pull requests to the published repositories refused — the same no-hand-edit contract ADR-637 D2 asserts. Externally consumable upstream becomes the seam face.

Any other first-party upstream path — pkg/**, cmd/**, plugin/** — is not externally consumable upstream, so it becomes the engine face and carries no external dependents. The k8s charter reserves core/ for the engine we RUN.

name_function._comment: Total and order-significant. Generated names are never typed by hand, so name length does not matter and a special case would only add a way to be wrong.
steps: strip the leading staging/src/k8s.io/ for a staging path; strip nothing otherwise
drop any pkg/apis/, pkg/ or tools/ segment — Go layout artifacts, not identity
name_function.examples_note: The second example is the one that matters: it exercises the pkg/apis/ drop, which is the only step that can silently change identity. The upstream module paths are a reading of upstream layout and are NOT confirmed against the pinned SourceModel — no package enumeration has run. They are here to pin the FUNCTION, which is exact, not to assert these modules exist at the pin.

face_constraint._comment: Why upstream- inside the existing faces, and not a new root directory.
face_constraint.rule: Both emit faces are depth-3 leaves that already match a root workspace member glob, so emitting costs ZERO root Cargo.toml edit and cannot serialize this lane against every other lane on that shared array. A novel root such as build/… or k8s/generated/… matches no glob, reds the workspace-glob-coverage gate with crate_dir_not_covered, and would need an ADR-authorized members exception this lane has no authority to write.
face_constraint.separation: The upstream- prefix is what makes a generated leaf mechanically separable from a hand-authored product port inside the same glob. It is the whole reason the four incumbent k8s/ports/*-api product crates need a classification field rather than a new address.

origin_classification._comment: The one cheap thing the incumbents actually need. Every tracked crate leaf under k8s/ and os/ is classified here, so a scan that finds zero hand-edited generated files can be distinguished from a scan that found nothing at all. Adding a leaf to the tree without adding its row here is the fail-closed condition below — an unclassified leaf is exactly the hole that makes a partition vacuous.

vocabulary.meaning: Hand-authored by this repository. Editing it is normal work. It is not emitted by any producer and MUST NOT fall inside a registered region.

Emitted into a registered regenerable region by that region's producer. Hand-editing it is a defect repaired in the rules, never in the emitted Rust. Every generated leaf MUST resolve to exactly one registered region.

origin_classification.scope: The two capabilities the port seam runs between: k8s/ (the destination ADR-638 D1 names) and os/ (the consumer). Other capabilities are out of scope for this file and are not silently claimed by it.
origin_classification.leaf_definition: A directory holding a tracked Cargo.toml at <capability>/<face>/<crate>/Cargo.toml.

repository_baseline.rebase_revalidation: Prior: restack onto origin/dev@9755cf50e after #1642 (18/42/60 + kernel-abi). 2026-08-11 re-measure on integ/os absorb tip vs merge-base 9a56538c74: +os/harness/attestation-relying-party +os/harness/oci-executor-oracle → k8s_leaves 18, os_leaves 44, total 62 (leaves[] already listed; census counts were stale at 43/61).

census.note: os/ is 40 crates under os/core/, 3 under os/harness/ (difftest-app + attestation-relying-party + oci-executor-oracle), 1 under os/ports/. Talos hand-port under os/core+harness remains first-party by ADR-638 D5 charter. os/ports/kernel-abi is the owned kernel-ABI seam (first-party port face), not generated. Re-measured on integ/os tip after #1931/#1932 absorb: git ls-files k8s/*/*/Cargo.toml os/*/*/Cargo.toml → 18/44/62.

fail_closed_conditions: Reject a tracked crate leaf under k8s/ or os/ that carries no row in origin_classification.leaves — an unclassified leaf is exactly the hole that makes a leaf-by-leaf boundary partition report a clean result over an unseen corpus.
Reject a row whose origin is outside the closed vocabulary.
Reject a leaf classified generated that resolves to no registered region, and reject a leaf classified first-party that falls inside a registered region path_prefix.
Reject a region registered without a producer or without all six receipt axes.
Reject two registered regions whose path prefixes overlap.
Reject an emit resolution where no rule matches, or where more than one matching rule holds the highest specificity_rank.

Reject an origin_classification.census total that disagrees with the census reproducer evaluated at HEAD — a stale census silently converts every count above into a claim about a tree that no longer exists.
not_claimed: That any producer, engine, rule pack or seam crate exists.
That any os/ to k8s/ dependency edge is authorized; ADR-638 D6 defers that to W0-G and this file does not pre-empt it.
That the candidate upstream module paths in emit_predicate.name_function.examples were confirmed against the pinned SourceModel.

That emit_predicate resolution (no-match / equal-highest-rank) is enforced by a reader today — that fail_closed condition remains specification until the producer evaluates it. Origin classification, region producer/receipt/overlap, and first-party-vs-generated coverage ARE enforced by ci-k8s-program-docs when this file is loaded.
